title: EventCheckResult
description: What the scheduler grammar checker answers for an event's text, the same from every entry point: the controller's MCP tool check_event, the studio editor, the backend's refusal of an event with errors (HTTP 400, {error: 'invalid-event', result}), ScriptEngine's calendarAction and the two CLIs. Produced by screenplan_contracts.event_grammar (Python) and @screenplan/script-actions scheduler-grammar-v2 (TypeScript), which agree on the conformance corpus in fixtures/event-grammar/. Each code, with its severity and message template, is listed in event-grammar-builtins.json. Lines are 1-based; columns are 1-based and counted in Unicode code points; the end is exclusive.

ok.description: True when there are no errors; warnings don't block.

grammar.description: Always 2: every event is grammar 2, with or without the optional `# ScreenPlan event (grammar 2)` header. 1 is no longer answered (it was text without the header, read as grammar 1, which no longer runs).

unchecked.description: Checks the context level couldn't run (a host that didn't answer, a source that couldn't be read): skipped, never guessed.

outline.description: What the event will run, in order: empty when the grammar level found errors.

code.description: Stable kebab-case code, the same in TypeScript and Python (event-grammar-builtins.json diagnostics).

fix.description: When there is exactly one obvious correction: the text that replaces the diagnostic's range.

line.description: The line of the statement (for an else branch or a finally block, of its first statement).

kind.description: For a sequence: what made it.

name.description: A command's built-in, a variable's name, or a sequence's header as written (onDestroy for the finally block).

inputs.description: The keyword arguments a script call passes: all it receives.

args.description: A command's or a def call's arguments, as written.

condition.description: An if command's condition, as written.

context.description: A with sequence's contexts, in order.

parallel.description: A with sequence whose contexts include parallel().
